title: Shared Mailbox Handling & Routing Guide
summary: How the Enquiries, Accounts and Learner Support shared mailboxes are monitored, categorised, prioritised and routed, including red-flag handling and what may be automated.
author: P002

version_history.change: First version covering Enquiries and Accounts
Learner Support mailbox and safeguarding red flags added
Category set and SLAs standardised; Automation & AI section added ahead of the Copilot rollout

blocks.p: Delcorn's three shared mailboxes are often the first contact an employer, apprentice or supplier has with us. This guide sets out who monitors each mailbox, how every email is **categorised**, **prioritised** and **routed**, the response times we commit to, and the red flags that must be handled before anything else.

It applies to everyone who monitors a shared mailbox, their backups, and anyone building an agent, rule or flow that reads these mailboxes. Every email must end up with **one category, one priority and one owner**.

bullets: Mailboxes are checked at **08:30, 12:30 and 16:00** on working days. The 08:30 check on Monday (and after a bank holiday) covers everything that arrived over the weekend.
Shared mailboxes are **not monitored out of hours**. Our auto-acknowledgement tells senders this and gives the 999 / Samaritans / safeguarding line details.
If the monitor is absent, the backup takes over that day. Learner Support must never go a working day unchecked.

numbered: **Scan for red flags first** (section 7): safeguarding or welfare concerns, phishing, bank-detail changes, data protection requests. Read the whole email - disclosures are often buried in an otherwise routine message.
**Categorise** using one of the twelve categories in section 4.
**Route** to the owner in the routing table (section 6) - forward or assign, and apply the matching Outlook category. Use the learner ID (LRN number), not a description of their circumstances.
**Acknowledge** where the routing table says so, using the approved templates.
**Mark duplicates and wrong-mailbox items** (section 8) and file or delete newsletters, auto-replies and spam.

blocks.h2: 6.1 What counts as a hot lead

bullets: A new employer wanting **10 or more** apprentices or learners, or
A levy-paying employer with a stated decision deadline or expiring levy funds, or
Any lead referred by the CEO or an executive director.
Hot leads go to the Senior Client Partner (public sector and health leads to the Client Partner for that sector) within **1 working day**, and are logged in PipelineHQ the same day.

blocks.callout: If an email suggests a learner may be at risk of harm - even one line in a message about something else - treat it as **Urgent**. Phone the DSL ({{person:P010}}) or Deputy DSL ({{person:P023}}) or the safeguarding line (020 7946 0199) straight away, then forward the email to safeguarding@delcorn.co.uk. If someone is in immediate danger, call 999.
blocks.title: Golden rule

bullets: Read every Learner Support email in full - disclosures are often buried in password resets or apologies for late work.
Apprentices aged 16-18 and adults at risk need particular care.
Do **not** reply asking for details, promise confidentiality, forward to coaches or employers, or post in Teams channels. The DSL decides what is shared and with whom.
Deal with the routine part of the email (e.g. an Aptiva reset) separately, without repeating the disclosure.

A learner who is missing or out of contact, reported by an employer, is a welfare check for the Deputy DSL the same day. Do not confirm anything about the learner to the employer until the safeguarding team has reviewed it.
Refer to learners by learner ID only in any onward message.
Typical signs: a lookalike or unknown sender domain, urgency or threats ('your account will be suspended'), generic greetings, links to sign-in pages, unexpected attachments.
Delcorn has **no forced password expiry** and our systems use Microsoft 365 sign-in - any 'password expires' email is suspicious.
Don't click, reply or forward to colleagues. Use the Outlook **Report** button and raise a FixDesk P1 ticket. If anyone has clicked, tell the Service Desk immediately.
Keep the email (don't just delete it) so the security team can investigate.
**Never** change supplier bank details because of an email, however genuine it looks.
Verify by phoning the supplier on the number **already held in Ledgerline** - never a number, letter or link in the email.
Compare the sender's domain with previous genuine emails from that supplier; lookalike domains (an added hyphen, a different ending) are common.
Pressure to act before a payment run or to 'confirm by email only' is a warning sign. Place a hold on payments to that supplier until verified.

A change needs two people: the Management Accountant makes it and the Finance Manager approves it after the call-back. Report suspected fraud to the Finance Manager and the Information Security Officer the same day.
Requests for **our** bank details should also be checked: give them only in the standard invoice format or by phone to a verified contact.
Any request for a copy of someone's own personal data is a subject access request (DSAR) - it doesn't have to use the words, and it can arrive in any mailbox.
Forward to the DPO ({{person:P036}}, dpo@delcorn.co.uk) the **same day**. Do not send any data, confirm what we hold or acknowledge on the DPO's behalf.
We must respond within **one calendar month of receipt** (e.g. received 30 October, due 30 November). The search includes emails, Teams chats and Copilot-generated documents.
Note: at Delcorn 'SAR' usually means the self-assessment report, so use 'DSAR' for data requests.
If the sender says they want to complain, or clearly wants a remedy for poor service, log it as a Complaint and route to the Quality Manager - even if it arrives in Accounts or Enquiries.
Billing disagreements are 'Invoices & payments' disputes unless the sender asks to complain.
Don't respond defensively from the shared mailbox; the investigating manager replies.

blocks.p: Only Marketing & Communications speaks to journalists. Forward media requests to {{person:P027}} immediately and do not reply with any comment, even 'no comment'.

blocks.h1: 8. Wrong mailbox, duplicates and personal data

bullets: **Wrong mailbox:** forward to the correct shared mailbox (or owner) and ask the sender to use it next time. Keep the original category and priority. Flag it 'wrong mailbox'.
**Duplicates:** if the same person sends the same request twice, merge them - one ticket, one reply. For invoices, check Ledgerline so the same invoice is never entered or paid twice.
**Personal data:** CVs, health information and learner details should not sit in a shared mailbox. Forward to the owner and delete.

blocks.p: Copilot, agents, Outlook rules and Power Automate flows may help us triage, but **a named person remains accountable for every email**. Automation must follow this guide and the AI Acceptable Use Policy.

blocks.callout: If an agent or flow is unsure, it must say so and leave the email for a person. A missed safeguarding disclosure or a paid fraudulent invoice costs far more than a slower triage.
